lead: # `scope::DENY_ALL` and `scope_verdict` — the write-scope vocabulary, already a crate.
# The RUNTIME CONFIG OVERLAY, so `write-locks.json` is read exactly as the app reads it. Verified
# rather than assumed: `bsc-config/build.rs` stages `../../src-tauri/data` into `$OUT_DIR/config-seed`
# and `src-tauri/build.rs` stages the same tree, with each file's own comment saying they are pinned
# together — so the embedded fallback here is byte-identical to `platform::config::load_str`'s.
# One `warn!` on an unreadable write-locks.json. Kept rather than dropped in the move: losing it would
# turn a degraded permission set into a silent one, which is the opposite of failing closed loudly.
# `bsc-perms` — the SESSION PERMISSION DERIVATION: role -> denied commands, tool rules, write scope,
# access env, bsc-agent permissions, and the hook chain.
# TAURI-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the dependency list is the proof rather than a claim. These eight
# modules were measured before they moved: their complete non-std import surface was `serde`,
# `bsc_util::scope`, and each other — no `tauri`, no `AppHandle`, no `State<>`, no `crate::app`, no
# `crate::console`. Adding a dependency here that is not pure would silently re-create the problem
# this crate exists to fix, so keep this list short and argue for anything new.
sections.name: [dependencies]

lead: # build.rs parses the committed graph store directly — see crates/graph-materialize/build.rs.
# THE SHARED CRATE ROOT — this crate owns no source file at all. See
# crates/graph-materialize/crate_root.rs; the crate's own docs come from its record.
# The MATERIALIZER, for its merged-store loader ONLY. `the_field_names_match_the_consumer` reads
# `bsc-agent`'s permissions record out of the committed graph store, which is one file plus
# `graph/records/<id>.json` per record (`epic-retire-json-ledgers-for-db-and-git-drivers`) — parsing
# the store file alone would report that record "missing from the graph store" while it sits in its
# own file. `graph_materialize` is what the BUILD reads, so going through it is what stops this test
# and the compiler disagreeing about which records exist. Dev-only: not propagated to anything that
# links this crate.
